done.summary:
You can now download the recommendation data from inside the app, and it built and passed every test below. The download is offered in Settings → Recommendations and on the Search page when there is nothing to suggest from.

How it works (new class RecData, available to QML as "RecData"):
- It reads manifest.json at the pinned tag v1. The constant kVersion has a comment on how to publish a new version: commit the files with a manifest saying version N, tag vN, push the tag, then raise the constant. The default address is https://raw.githubusercontent.com/droidboy08-hub/Monolist-data/v1/. MONOLIST_REC_DATA_URL replaces it with any URL or a local folder.
- Each file is written to "<file>.part" and hashed as it arrives, 1 MB per turn of the event loop, so the window never freezes. Downloads and checks of files already on disk both work this way.
- A file is renamed into place only if its size and SHA-256 match. A file already present at the right size is hashed first and kept if it matches. A leftover .part is never reused, so an interrupted download carries on from the last whole file.
- Every path in the manifest is checked against a strict pattern (EmbeddingData/ or GraphData/ plus a plain file name). The manifest's name and version are checked, and free disk space is checked before anything is written.
- Errors are plain sentences. A missing manifest says "The list of files is not at <url>. The data may not have been published there yet". A bad file says "GraphData/AE.sqlite did not match its checksum, so it was refused…", with separate wording for a file that arrives too short or too long.
- Files go to <data folder>/recommendations/v1, next to the SQLite database, so MONOLIST_DATA_DIR moves them too. When the download is whole, the catalogue setting points at v1/EmbeddingData and the graph setting is cleared, so GraphData is found beside the catalogue.
- Remove first makes the recommender close its files (the catalogue is memory-mapped and Windows won't delete a mapped file), then deletes only v1, and its parent folder if that is left empty.
- A failed first attempt leaves no empty folders behind.

Recommender changes:
- `useDirectories()` sets both folders with one reload instead of two.
- `release(folder)` clears any setting that points into that folder and reloads.
- `isInside()` checks whether one path is under another.
- A new `dataLoaded()` signal fires once the worker holds only what the settings name, with no load still queued.

What you see:
- A shared panel, RecDataPanel.qml, has seven states: nothing downloaded, downloading, part-way, failed, removing, downloaded, and downloaded but not in use.
- The title states the state and the buttons name the action: "DOWNLOAD RECOMMENDATION DATA — 100 MB" (red), CANCEL, CARRY ON / TRY AGAIN, USE IT and REMOVE, with the 2px progress bar used on the Downloads page. In a narrow window the buttons move below the text.
- Settings gets small "DATA" and "CATALOGUE" labels; the typed folder fields still work.
- The required credit (DataCredit.qml) appears under Recommendations and in About, with links to the Monolist-data repo, Embeat 45M, MusicBrainz, ListenBrainz, the MetaBrainz Foundation and each licence.
- An empty Search page now explains why it is empty and shows the same panel, plus a link "OR CHOOSE A FOLDER IN SETTINGS →".

README: a licence line saying the data lives in the Monolist-data repo under its own licences, the new self-tests, MONOLIST_REC_DATA_URL, the storage path, and recdata.* in the file list.

Steps 1 to 4 of the Last.fm build order are done and committed as b6dda47 (build succeeds, qmllint clean).

(1) Repo hygiene and UI scaffolding.
- .gitignore now ignores cookies*.txt, *.cookies, secrets/, Secrets.plist and apicredentials.h. No tracked file matched any of them.
- ServiceRow gains `built`, `serviceState` (off, waiting, connected, expired, error or unavailable), `accountName` and `statusLine`, plus the signals connectRequested, disconnectRequested and cancelRequested.
  - When built, the button becomes CONNECT, CANCEL, DISCONNECT, RECONNECT or TRY AGAIN. It is hidden when unavailable.
  - `built` hides the "Not built yet" footer.
  - The property is `serviceState`, not `state`, because every QML Item already has a `state` property and this would shadow it.
- Settings copy:
  - Last.fm step 3 now says: half the track or four minutes, whichever comes first; 30 seconds or less never counts; Last.fm is also told what is playing now; nothing else is sent.
  - Last.fm step 2 now says the session key is encrypted.
  - YouTube Music lines are fixed as the design lists: "encrypted with your Windows sign-in (the Keychain on a Mac)", the sign-out wording, and the new "A session lasts days to weeks" step. The caution line is unchanged.
  - The Connections note now depends on the Last.fm row's state.
  - The Last.fm row reads its state and status line from a new QML singleton, `LastFm`. With no key it shows "This build has no Last.fm key." Both rows still say "Not built yet".

(2) SecretStore.
- Windows backend: DPAPI (CryptProtectData with CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN), links crypt32.
- Each secret is a file saved with QSaveFile in a `secrets` folder beside the database, so MONOLIST_DATA_DIR moves it too.
- The file starts with a magic/version header. The DPAPI entropy includes the secret's name, so a file copied over another name does not decrypt.
- A damaged file reads as Corrupt, and read never returns a partial value. Deleting something already gone counts as success. Names are validated, including Windows device names such as "con".
- secretstore_win.cpp is entirely inside `#ifdef Q_OS_WIN`.
- On other platforms, a fallback in secretstore.cpp (guarded by `!Q_OS_WIN && !MONOLIST_HAVE_KEYCHAIN`) returns Unavailable with "Keeping a sign-in safely is not available on this platform yet."

(3) Build-time credentials.
- cmake/apicredentials.cmake reads MONOLIST_LASTFM_API_KEY and MONOLIST_LASTFM_SHARED_SECRET from the environment on every build, like the build number, and writes build/generated/apicredentials.h. The header is rewritten only when it changes.
- `-D` values are also accepted; they are fixed when CMake configures.
- A value containing anything other than letters and digits, or only one of the two being set, gives a warning that names the variable but never its value, and the build proceeds with no key.
- CMake prints only "this build has a Last.fm key" or "this build has no Last.fm key". The values never reach CMakeCache.txt or build.ninja on the environment path.
- CMakeLists.txt changes are one additive block after the buildinfo section: target_sources, crypt32, and the credentials step.

(4) LastFmApi (src/lastfm.h/.cpp), with no network code yet.
- `signature()`: parameters sorted by UTF-8 bytes, format and callback excluded, secret appended, lowercase hex MD5.
- `sign()`: adds api_sig, then format=json, replacing any stale ones.
- `formBody()`: every name and value goes through QUrl::toPercentEncoding.
- `parseReply()`: Last.fm's error number decides whatever the HTTP status. Anything else that is not a 2xx JSON object is treated as Retry. Scrobble items are read whether Last.fm sends one object or an array, and counts whether sent as numbers or strings.
- Mapping: 9 means reauthenticate; 10, 13 and 26 hold the queue; 11 and 16 retry; 29 is rate-limited; 14 keeps waiting; 15 restarts sign-in; everything else is rejected.
- Per-item ignored codes: 0 accepted, 1 to 4 dropped, 5 try tomorrow.
- The API key and secret are private to lastfm.cpp.

Self-test flags `--secret-test` and `--lastfm-test` run before the database opens, with no window, and exit 0 only when every check passes. `--diag` now prints whether there is a key (never the key). README documents the flags, the key setup and the secrets folder.

findings.problem: Last.fm error 8 ("Operation failed. Most likely the backend service failed. Please try again") falls into the default branch of outcomeForError and becomes Outcome::Rejected. parseReply lets the JSON error number override the HTTP status, so an HTTP 5xx carrying {"error":8} is Rejected too. In Scrobbler::handleBatch (scrobbler.cpp:850-862), a Rejected batch of more than one is split into singles, and a Rejected single is removeRows()'d with no retry. So a transient backend failure deletes queued scrobbles for good. This contradicts scrobbler.h's own table ("no answer, 5xx, 11, 16: kept, backoff") and the design's "drop only those that fail non-retryably".
findings.scenario: 120 scrobbles are queued, e.g. after being offline. Last.fm has a backend hiccup and answers every request with HTTP 500 {"error":8}. Batch 1 (50) is refused and split into m_singles. flush() then fires the 50 singles back to back (QTimer::singleShot(0) after each answer); each is answered 8 and deleted. Batches 2 and 3 go the same way, so the whole queue is gone within a minute. Normal use hits it too: a single freshly queued scrobble answered 8 once is deleted immediately.
findings.fix: Treat 8 (and any error that arrives with a 5xx status) as Retry, i.e. back off and keep the rows. Keep split-and-drop only for errors that are item-specific (6). Alternatively, drop a single only after its attempts column reaches a limit instead of on the first refusal.

findings.problem: Tracks started from a Home card or a Search suggestion carry no primaryArtist, and the "artist" they carry is not an artist. HomeView passes card.subtitle, the raw joined subtitle runs ("Rick Astley • 1.6B views", "Song • Artist"; see innertube.cpp:298 and the comment at :170), as the artist to Player.playSource. Recommender::play (recommender.cpp:327) passes track.artist, which is every credit joined with ", ". playSource has no primaryArtist parameter, so Scrobbler::scrobbleArtist (scrobbler.cpp:557-559) falls back to `artist`. Last.fm is then sent that string as the artist, both as now-playing and as the scrobble.
findings.scenario: Connected to Last.fm, the user clicks a video card in a Home carousel ("Music videos for you"). Half-way through, a scrobble is queued with artist "Rick Astley • 1.6B views" (or "Song • Artist" for a song card), creating a bogus artist on the user's public profile. A Search suggestion for a duet is scrobbled as "Bruno Mars, Lady Gaga", the exact case the design said to avoid. Library, liked and download rows also lack primaryArtist and send the joined credit.
findings.fix: Parse primaryArtist for cards in parseCard (firstArtistRun over the subtitle runs), expose it in Catalog's card map, and pass it through playSource with a new parameter or a map. Pass track.primaryArtist in Recommender::play. As a guard, have scrobbleArtist refuse or trim artist strings containing " • ".

findings.problem: ListenTracker::restart(), called from Previous past 3 s, re-runs begin(m_track, ...), which resets m_durationMs to the queue row's listed durationMs and discards the length mpv reported. After a seek, mpv does not report the length again: MpvEngine emits durationChanged only when it differs from m_duration, which only load() and stop() reset. For a track whose listed length is 0, thresholdMs(0) stays -1, so the replayed listen can never qualify.
findings.scenario: The user plays a song from a Home card. Player.playSource(..., 0, ...) gives it durationMs 0, and mpv then reports 3:30. 20 s in they press Previous and listen to the whole song. The first listen (20 s) never qualified, and the replay has m_durationMs = 0, so the song is never scrobbled at all. Self-test 11 misses this because its song has a listed length.
findings.fix: In restart(), keep the known length, e.g. `const qint64 known = m_durationMs; begin(m_track, m_chosenByUser); if (known > 0) m_durationMs = known;`. Or have PlaybackController call m_listen.setDuration(m_duration) after restart().

findings.problem: The F04 change closes the play event at Previous. closePlayEvent then puts the song's key in m_finalisedThisSession, so the replay's event is treated as "returned to in the same sitting". The existing rule at :721-725 then upgrades any replay label above 0 to 1.0. As a result, restarting a song and then skipping it after at least 10% is recorded as a full listen. Before this change, the one event was closed at the final playhead and stayed at 0.2.
findings.scenario: The user starts a 3:00 song, presses Previous at 0:05, listens 20 s more, then presses Next. play_events gets row 1 (5 s, label 0.0, skipped) and row 2 (repeat_in_session=1, 20 s, ratio 0.11, label 0.2 upgraded to 1.0). Taste weighs it +1.0 against -0.2, and buildShelves' saidYes (label >= 0.6) seeds a "Because you played ..." shelf from a song the listener skipped. The old code recorded one row with label 0.2 (neutral).
findings.fix: When previous() closes the event for a restart, do not add the key to m_finalisedThisSession (or open the replay with a flag that skips the upgrade). A restart is not the "return in the same sitting" the upgrade rule is for.

findings.problem: remove() waits for the worker to let go only when release() changed a setting. If the settings already point elsewhere while the worker still has v1 mapped or open (a reload queued behind a running build), removeFiles() runs at once. QDir::removeRecursively then deletes what it can, including manifest.json, and leaves the mapped embeat_*.bin and any open shards. With the manifest gone, refreshDiskState reports neither installed nor partial. The panel then hides REMOVE and offers TRY AGAIN, which re-downloads, and after a restart the leftover ~100 MB is invisible to the app.
findings.scenario: The download is in use and a build is running (e.g. the first build of the session reading every shard). The user types their own folder into CATALOGUE; setDataDirectory queues a reload behind the build. They then press REMOVE on the now "Not in use" panel. release() returns false, and the files are deleted while still mapped. The result is "Some of it could not be removed", the manifest is gone, the bins stay, and there is no REMOVE button.
findings.fix: Have remove() also wait for dataLoaded while a load is still pending (expose m_loadsPending > 0, or always reload and wait). In removeFiles, delete manifest.json last and only when everything else went, so a partial removal still shows as partial with REMOVE.

findings.problem: `LastFmApi::endpoint()` reads MONOLIST_LASTFM_URL in every build, Release included. It accepts any http or https host, and `call()` sends the build's api_key/api_sig plus the REAL session key `sk` from SecretStore there. The loopback-only check exists only inside `--scrobble-send-test`, not on this path. That breaks the design rule that the session key goes only to ws.audioscrobbler.com.
findings.scenario: The owner sets `$env:MONOLIST_LASTFM_URL='http://127.0.0.1:8765/2.0/'` (as the README and lastfm-mock.ps1 show) or sets it persistently with setx, then runs the app normally without MONOLIST_DATA_DIR. The stored real `lastfm.session` is posted in plain HTTP to whatever process holds that port, which on a shared machine can be another user. If that server answers error 9 (for example the mock's `/err9/` path), `Scrobbler::expire()` also deletes the real key.
findings.fix: Honour the override only for a loopback host. Better still, honour it only when `setTestAccount()` has been called, so the build's key and a SecretStore session are never sent to anything but https://ws.audioscrobbler.com/2.0/.

findings.problem: A hostile cookies.txt can trigger undefined behaviour. The expiry column is parsed with `toDouble()` and then cast with `qint64(expires)`, and the only check is `expires < 0`. A value like `1e300` parses as finite and valid (so does `inf` with Qt's parser), and converting a double outside qint64's range is undefined in C++.
findings.scenario: A cookies.txt line such as `.youtube.com\tTRUE\t/\tTRUE\t1e300\tSAPISID\tx`. On x86-64 the cast gives INT64_MIN, so the cookie is kept as a session cookie. On arm64 (the macOS build) it saturates to INT64_MAX. Either way the result is undefined and the stored expiry is wrong.
findings.fix: Reject non-finite values and clamp before casting, e.g. `if (!std::isfinite(expires) || expires > 253402300799.0) { ++unreadable; continue; }`, then cast.

findings.problem: Requests that carry the account set raw `Cookie` and `Authorization` (SAPISIDHASH) headers but keep Qt's default redirect policy, NoLessSafeRedirectPolicy, which follows any https to https redirect. Qt builds the redirected request as a copy of the original, raw headers included. The jar replaces Cookie only when it holds cookies for the new URL, and Authorization is never stripped. After a redirect, `absorbCookies` also records the target host's Set-Cookie without a Domain as music.youtube.com host-only cookies.
findings.scenario: music.youtube.com answers an authed `youtubei/v1/browse` or `account/account_menu` with a 3xx to another https host, for example a consent or sign-in interstitial. The session cookies and SAPISIDHASH are resent there, and that host's cookies are merged into the YouTube Music jar and saved to SecretStore. In practice the target would be a Google host, but it breaks the "only youtube.com over https" invariant. I could not confirm Qt 6.11's exact header handling from here because no Qt source is installed.
findings.fix: When `account != 0`, set `request.setAttribute(QNetworkRequest::RedirectPolicyAttribute, QNetworkRequest::ManualRedirectPolicy)` and treat a 3xx as no verdict (Checking) or retry anonymously (IfSignedIn).

findings.problem: The downloaded data is trusted on the strength of a mutable git tag alone. Every SHA-256 is checked against manifest.json fetched from the same `.../Monolist-data/v1/` location, and nothing in the binary pins the manifest itself. The comment's guarantee that "every build fetches exactly the files it was written for" is a publishing policy the code does not enforce.
findings.scenario: Tag v1 is moved, whether by a force-push to fix a data mistake or by a compromised owner or collaborator account. Every installed build then accepts the new manifest, downloads the files it lists, hash-checks them against that same manifest, and points the recommender at them. The recommender memory-maps the catalogue and opens the graph shards read-only as SQLite. Existing header validation and READONLY limit the damage, but the integrity promise is gone.
findings.fix: Next to kVersion, compile in the expected SHA-256 of manifest.json (or of its `files` array) and refuse any manifest that does not match. Publishing a new version already requires a new build, so this adds no extra step.

I also scanned the self-tests for clang/libc++ compile risks and read the latest build log (scratchpad\scrobble-build.log: clean apart from a pre-existing nodiscard warning).

Verified OK:
- Downloader, cancel mid-file: disconnect, then abort and deleteLater; the .part is closed and removed; a stale verify or pump is caught by the generation check and the m_reply check, including a cancel from inside a progress handler.
- Downloader, app quit mid-download: ~RecData calls stopTransfers; the QNAM is a child, deleted after connections are torn down; the zero-timers have `this` as context.
- Last.fm connect flow: the poll timer is a member and stopped on every exit path; all callbacks guard with QPointer and a generation; LastFmApi is destroyed after Scrobbler (stack order), so late replies hit a null QPointer.
- scrobble_queue: all SQL runs on the main thread (Scrobbler, the PlaybackController signals, LastFmApi replies); only the recommender worker uses a second thread, and it does no SQL.
- YtmSession: it outlives every other InnerTube; the hook is cleared in its destructor and the check InnerTube is deleted there first; QML singletons are all declared before the QQmlApplicationEngine, so they are destroyed after it.
- Portability: all DPAPI code is inside #ifdef Q_OS_WIN, with a fallback that compiles when !Q_OS_WIN && !MONOLIST_HAVE_KEYCHAIN; crypt32 is linked only under if(WIN32); no backslash paths or .exe names outside comments and test strings; the case-insensitive path compare is guarded; format strings cast to long long; cookie parsing uses uchar, so it does not depend on whether char is signed; no structured bindings captured in lambdas (clang < 16 rejects that in C++17); the tests include <tuple>/<iterator> for std::make_tuple/std::size; the Qt APIs used (QTimeZone::UTC, SingleShotConnection, QList::removeIf, QNetworkInformation) are within the 6.6 floor.

Not verified: no macOS or clang compile was possible. HTTP/2 honouring setReadBufferSize was not checked; if it does not, that is a memory spike only, not reported. Neither race was reproduced at runtime; both findings come from reading the code.

findings.problem: remove() only waits for the recommender to let go of the files when release() finds a setting that points into v1. It does not check whether the worker still holds the files. If the catalogue setting was just moved away from v1, release() returns false and removeFiles() runs at once. At that moment the worker may still have v1 memory-mapped and its SQLite shards open, because the load for the new folder is queued behind a build that is still running.
findings.scenario: On Windows, the panel shows 'Not in use' with REMOVE, or the user types their own folder in CATALOGUE and then clicks REMOVE. That click moves focus, so onEditingFinished calls setDataDirectory() and a reload is queued. If a build on the v1 catalogue is still running (the loaded handler starts one after every load, and the first build of a session reads every shard), release() returns false. removeRecursively() then fails on the mapped .bin files and the open GraphData shards, but it does delete manifest.json. refreshDiskState() then reports not installed and not partial, so the panel shows 'The download did not finish' with only TRY AGAIN. REMOVE is gone, and up to about 100 MB stays orphaned in <data>/recommendations/v1. The same thing happens if a reload that points back into v1 is queued while a removal is waiting for dataLoaded.
findings.fix: Have Recommender expose whether a load is pending (m_loadsPending > 0) or which folders the worker last loaded, and make RecData::remove() wait for dataLoaded whenever a load is pending or the worker's last-loaded catalogue or graph is inside folderPath(), not only when a setting points there. It is also worth deleting manifest.json last, or only after everything else is gone, so a partial removal still reads as 'partial' and keeps the REMOVE button.

findings.problem: Remove clears the catalogue and graph settings first (Recommender::release) and deletes the files only later, when dataLoaded arrives. If the app quits in between, ~Recommender interrupts the worker, the release load returns early without emitting loaded, and RecData (destroyed first) never runs removeFiles. On the next launch setRecommender() sees the files installed and both settings empty, so it calls use() and quietly re-adopts the data the user asked to remove.
findings.scenario: The user opens Settings soon after launch or after USE IT, while the post-load build is still running, clicks REMOVE (the panel shows REMOVING…), and closes the window before that build finishes. The next launch shows 'Recommendation data, version 1… Search suggests from it', and the files are still in use.
findings.fix: Record the pending removal durably, for example a 'rec.removePending' setting written in remove() and cleared in removeFiles(). At startup, before the adoption rule, delete the folder if the flag is set (nothing has mapped it yet). Alternatively, skip the adoption rule while the flag is set.
